relevance_note: Case report of a Japanese family with "two cases of autoinflammatory disease which exhibit an identical novel TNFAIP3 mutation" (proband and younger sister), described individually.
method_note: Read the full paper (a short letter; no tables in the Markdown) and built the JSON with a small Python script in scratch; all values were chosen by reading, not transcribed by script. In scope: the proband ('patient', the paper's own most frequent term; also called 'the proband'), his younger sister (tested carrier, affected), his mother (affected, not reported as tested, deceased) and his father (tested negative, unaffected). Out of scope: 'the younger brothers of the proband without symptoms' (untested and unaffected, number not stated) get no rows. No variant row for the mother: the paper only says the father's negative test 'suggest[s]' maternal origin; she was not reported as sequenced. Additional file 1 (Table S1, laboratory data) is not in the Markdown; the 'Supplementary material' section holds only back matter, so 'There were no abnormalities except elevated levels of C-reactive protein (CRP)' was not used to exclude any checklist item. Uveitis is excluded for the proband, but per the narrow/broad rule the checklist item 'uveitis or other ocular inflammation' is left not reported. Gastric mucosal erosions were mapped to 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (observed). The sister's 'similar symptoms' are non-specific, so all her checklist items are not reported. Contradictions in the paper: (1) cDNA given as 'C596_598 del A' in the text (capital C, no period, recorded as printed) but as 'c597-598 T deletion' in the Fig. 1 legend (which notes the sequence is shown with the reverse primer); the text form was used. (2) The variant is called a frameshift several times but 'a novel heterozygous missense mutation' once; recorded as frameshift. (3) Protein printed as 'Cys200Alafsx16', 'C200Afs*16', 'C200A fs*16' and 'C200A'; 'Cys200Alafsx16' recorded. (4) Proband timeline: '17-year-old' at referral with a 3-year history, then 'Three years later' admitted; age at last evaluation therefore left not reported; onset 'at 14 years old' attributed to the proband (the sister's onset is 11 years). (5) 'no abnormalities except elevated' CRP versus positive ANA and elevated cytokines in the same paragraph. Inheritance recorded as 'inherited maternal' from the authors' hedged statement ('suggesting that these mutations were maternally derived'); the mother was not tested. Functional assay (immunoblot) was done on the proband's PBMCs only; it is repeated on the sister's variant row with that caveat. HLA-B (not B51) not recorded (not a schema field).
